Forty years I've been working this land. I know its quirks — when it's dry in the subsoil even when the surface looks fine, which rows get waterlogged, where the aphids always show up first. At 65, I pace myself. Two of my sons work in the city, so I manage most of the field labor myself or with my wife, and I hire day laborers only at peak times like garlic harvest and cotton picking.

My wheat-maize double crop is the foundation — I won't touch that. It runs on 8 mu and it's reliable income with predictable costs. I know it cold. For the remaining 6 mu, garlic goes on 3 mu for the winter slot because prices at the county market have stayed decent and I can sell locally without trucking far. Cotton takes the last 3 mu — I've grown it my whole life, but I'm keeping it small because hand-harvesting cotton is the hardest work on the farm and I can't count on family help the way I used to.

**Wheat:** I'll use an improved variety from the county seed station — my neighbor switched two years ago and his yields jumped. Base fertilizer goes in before sowing, top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I'll irrigate at sowing if soil moisture is short, then jointing, heading, and grain fill — four times total. Rotary till right after maize comes off in early October before I plant. I expect 450 kg/mu.

**Maize:** Hybrid seed, same as every year — haven't used anything else in two decades. I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June, no extra tillage needed. Bigger nitrogen doses than wheat because maize is a heavy feeder. I'll spray once for corn borer around the V6 stage and check again at silking. Three irrigations unless the summer rains save me some well water. I expect 550 kg/mu.

**Garlic:** I plant local traditional variety in late September. Buyers at Quzhou market know the flavor and pay better for it than for the outside varieties. Garlic wants a lot of potassium, so I load up on that. It needs consistent moisture through the dry winter and spring, so I'll irrigate five times. Spray for purple blotch and rust three times — I've lost a crop to that before and I won't again. Harvest in late May, just before things get crazy with wheat. I expect 900 kg/mu.

**Cotton:** Plant late April after last frost, improved hybrid seed — Bt varieties cut down some of my spraying but I still need five pesticide passes for bollworm, aphids, and spider mites. Cotton soil I'll plough in spring to break up compaction. Four irrigations, heavier in flowering and boll-setting. It's the hardest crop I manage, but I know it and the cash comes in a different season from wheat and garlic so it smooths out my income. I expect 220 kg/mu seed cotton.
